back: The output at which total revenue equals total costs, so profit is zero.
Selling price − variable cost per unit.
Output × contribution per unit − fixed costs.
(Fixed costs + target profit) ÷ contribution per unit.
Actual output − break-even output (units); ÷ actual output × 100 for a percentage.
Fixed-cost line horizontal; total cost starts at the fixed-cost level; total revenue starts at the origin; they meet at break-even; loss to the left, profit to the right.
Higher price or lower variable cost lowers break-even; higher fixed costs raise it. A price cut helps only if extra sales outweigh the lower contribution.
Assumes constant price and variable cost, all output sold and fixed costs fixed; relies on forecasts; hard for many products.
